scores.claim_text: OAS primarily targets defense, homeland security, and public safety customers. A significant portion of revenue depends on government customers.
scores.M_check: USAspending federal contracts/grants for Ondas, Airobotics, American Robotics, Sentrycs, Roboteam (2020-2026)
scores.M_value: Direct 'Ondas' substring matches = 10 awards / $206K, but ALL 10 are HONDASHOKAI Y.K. (a Japanese supplier — plywood, freezer boxes, flow meter calibration in Iwakuni). Zero awards to Ondas Inc., Ondas Holdings, Ondas Networks, Ondas Autonomous Systems. Airobotics: 0 contracts, 0 grants. Sentrycs: 0. Roboteam: 0. American Robotics: 1 DHS award ($167K) for 'UAS sniffer package'. Ondas grant hits are foreign-NGO substring noise (FONDASYON KOLE ZEPOL, etc.).
scores.interpretation: Apply Layer 3 Rule 7 + Heuristic 9: company positions itself as a US-defense / homeland-security / public-safety contractor and explicitly tells investors that 'a significant portion of our business... involves sales to government customers, including defense, homeland security, and public safety agencies.' USAspending shows essentially zero federal contract obligations across the parent and every named acquired defense subsidiary (Airobotics, Sentrycs, Roboteam, 4M Defense). The only direct hit, American Robotics, has a single $168K DHS award — a rounding error relative to the ~$50M of revenue claimed for 2025 ($27.8M + $5.4M + smaller). HARD CONTRADICTION. The $27.8M anchor customer is therefore extremely unlikely to be a US federal defense buyer; if it is foreign or commercial, the marketing-vs-reality gap (military-base protection, mobile air defense, force protection, US DoD budgets) is material.

scores.claim_text: Two customers accounted for $27.8M (55%) and $5.4M (11%) of 2025 revenue (vs. $3.8M / $1.9M / $0.7M for top 3 customers in 2024 — a 7x+ jump in concentration revenue), with one customer = 73% of A/R at year-end.
scores.M_check: EDGAR fulltext for 'Ondas', 'Airobotics', 'Optimus System' restricted to defense primes and Class I railroads
scores.M_value: Zero mentions across tested counterparty CIKs: LMT=0, NOC=0, RTX=0, GD=0, LHX=0, BA=0, UP=0, CSX=0, NSC=0, Berkshire=0, CN=0, CP/CPKC=0, Wabtec=0. Ondas EDGAR total 506 / Ondas Networks 280 / FullMAX 168 / Airobotics 119 / Optimus System 95 / Iron Drone Raider 107 — top hits in all searches are Ondas's own filings; no external filer surfaced. Anchor customer is undisclosed in 10-K, and no counterparty SEC filing corroborates Ondas as a vendor.
scores.interpretation: Apply Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold): a $27.8M relationship is generally NOT material to a Class I railroad ($25B-$30B revenue) or a top-5 defense prime ($30B-$70B revenue), so absence of mention there alone is not dispositive. However, combined with the 73% A/R concentration and revenue identity unknown, this is a watch item — particularly because (a) prior-year revenue concentration was sub-$4M largest customer and (b) the largest 2025 customer paid only a fraction of what was invoiced (73% A/R = ~$20M still outstanding). Score MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: the disclosure itself is the concern (collection risk + concentration), not yet a falsified claim.

scores.claim_text: Ondas Networks IP forms the core of IEEE 802.16; FullMAX is a patented SDR platform for industrial wireless.
scores.M_value: 11 total applications, 3 granted patents, all assigned to 'Ondas Networks Inc.' Titles include 'Broadband Wireless Communication for Mission Critical IoT' (granted 2024-06-25) and 'Automatic Packet Field Suppression in Broadband Wireless Communications Systems' (granted 2019-12-03). CPC codes H04W (wireless networks) and H04L (data transmission) confirm 802.16-relevant technology area.
scores.interpretation: Apply Heuristic 8: 3 granted patents is below the n_granted>=5 PASS threshold, but every single granted patent and pending application is directly in the claimed technology area (broadband wireless / mission-critical IoT / SDR), all under Ondas Networks Inc. as applicant. The IP claim is real and on-topic. PASS, with note that the patent portfolio is thin (3 granted) for a company positioning as the sole 802.16s vendor; the moat is real but narrow.

scores.claim_text: Airobotics provides the Optimus System (autonomous drone, FAA Type Certified 2023) and Iron Drone Raider (autonomous interceptor). Airobotics is a deployed defense-tech subsidiary.
scores.M_check: USPTO ODP assignee search for 'Airobotics' and 'American Robotics' (the FAA-type-certified entity)
scores.M_value: Airobotics: 4 total applications, 1 granted ('Landing and Charging System for Drones', granted 2021-02-09); the other three (payload exchange, positioning/locking, landing platform) were abandoned for failure to respond to office actions. American Robotics: 34 applications, 10 granted patents, all on drone aircraft / data collection / threat detection / autonomous landing topics. Combined: 11 granted patents in claimed drone technology area.
scores.interpretation: Per Heuristic 8 (n_granted>=5 with claimed-category hit = PASS), the combined Airobotics + American Robotics portfolio of 11 granted patents directly in autonomous drone systems exceeds the PASS threshold. FAA Type Certification claim is consistent with the technology depth shown by American Robotics' 10-patent portfolio. PASS. Caveat: Airobotics' OWN portfolio is weak (1 granted, 3 abandoned), so the Airobotics-branded products lean on what American Robotics built pre-acquisition.

scores.claim_text: Ondas Networks has historically targeted North American freight rail (AAR, Class I railroads) as the early adoption market for FullMAX; industry bodies including AAR adopted IEEE 802.16.
scores.M_check: EDGAR fulltext for 'FullMAX', 'Ondas Networks', '802.16t' across all filers and restricted to Class I railroads + Wabtec (the rail PTC vendor)
scores.M_value: FullMAX total EDGAR hits = 168, all top hits are Ondas's own filings. Restricted to UP (CIK 0000100885) = 0 hits; CSX = 0; NSC = 0; BRK (parent of BNSF) = 0; Wabtec (the dominant rail PTC equipment OEM) = 0; CN = 0; CP/CPKC = 0. Ondas Networks total = 280 hits, all top hits are Ondas's own filings.
scores.interpretation: Apply Heuristic 7 with caveat: railroads ARE the claimed end customer and FullMAX/AAR/802.16 deployment is the company's headline rail proof-point. A genuine Class I railroad rolling out FullMAX over a multi-year PTC/next-gen-comms program would typically appear in 10-K risk factors, capex disclosures, or vendor-concentration mentions; total absence across the five US Class I railroads and Wabtec (the prime integrator) suggests FullMAX has not achieved material commercial traction in the rail vertical despite being marketed as such since 2017+. This is similar to the LMT/NOC counterparty-silence pattern but stronger because the claim explicitly names the rail vertical as the lead adoption market. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY (not RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE because (a) some pilot/trial activity may exist below SEC-disclosure materiality and (b) AAR did publish 802.16 standards work, just not a deployed Ondas product).

scores.claim_text: Sentrycs (CoRF CUAS), Roboteam (UGV), 4M Defense (demining) are deployed defense capabilities feeding the US DoD / Western military customer base.
scores.M_check: USAspending federal contracts for Sentrycs and Roboteam (2020-2026)
scores.M_value: Sentrycs: 0 federal awards. Roboteam: 0 federal awards. (Both queried unrestricted by awarding agency — covers DoD, DHS, State, every federal buyer.)
scores.interpretation: Per Heuristic 9: company markets Sentrycs and Roboteam as integrated CUAS/UGV defense platforms that can be deployed for 'defense, homeland security, and public safety customers' and ties them directly to US DoD spending ('U.S. defense budget surging to nearly $748 million for small unmanned systems in FY2026'). Zero federal contract obligations for either named subsidiary is a HARD CONTRADICTION on the stated US-defense positioning. Could reflect that these companies sell to Israel / UAE / foreign militaries (consistent with Israel HQ + UAE litigation footprint disclosed in legal proceedings) — but the 10-K's plain-language framing implies US-government customers. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE on the implied US-federal-customer scope; would moderate if framed as foreign-only.

scores.claim_text: Ondas Networks and OAS funded prior-year working capital through related-party convertible notes from C&P (Joseph Popolo, former director). $1B raised Jan 2026 + $829M raised in 2025 effectively eliminates near-term solvency risk.
scores.M_check: Internal filing review — disclosed related-party transactions in Notes 18/19
scores.M_value: Disclosed: C&P (Joseph Popolo) provided $2M Common Stock subscription Feb 2024, $2.5M Networks convertible notes, $2M OAS convertible notes (converted to OAS Common Stock Dec 17, 2025 in OAS Exchange), $1.5M Networks Secured Note. Privet Ventures (Eric Brock, CEO) bought $1M OAS convertible note (converted Jan 5, 2026). 2025 Offerings raised $830M net + $1B Jan 2026 raise leaves the company with $594M cash at 12/31/2025 + $959M net from Jan 2026 = ~$1.5B+ liquidity.
scores.interpretation: Pattern is consistent with the 'stock-for-services / vendor-equity-payable' related-party-funding fingerprint from prior backtests (SRFM, LILM) when small — director and CEO personally funding the operating subsidiaries via converted notes that exchange into parent stock is structurally unusual. However, the post-conversion balance sheet is robust ($1.5B liquidity, $13M total debt) and the related-party position is fully unwound. PASS as a near-term solvency matter; related-party governance is a watch item, not a falsified claim. (Note per Heuristic 'divergence_not_solvency': a balance-sheet PASS does not rule out operational underdelivery — see C1, C5, C6.)

scores.claim_text: Ondas has ~15 principal facilities in 4 countries: 4 US locations (MA, MD, FL, CA), 11 outside the US (primarily Israel).
scores.M_check: EPA FRS facility lookup across plausible state/subsidiary combinations
scores.M_value: 0 facilities returned across all eight EPA queries (Ondas, Airobotics, American Robotics, Sentrycs, Roboteam across MA / MD / FL).
scores.interpretation: Per Heuristic 1, EPA FRS only covers EPA-regulated facilities; light defense electronics and drone assembly are typically below FRS thresholds. Absence here is consistent with the cohort calibration note, not a falsification signal. UNVERIFIABLE via this source; would need lease filings or another property registry to confirm.
